name: What is the difference between a three-season and a four-season sunroom addition?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a three-season and a four-season sunroom addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: A four-season sunroom is built as a fully integrated extension of your living space, whereas a three-season room is designed primarily for spring through autumn. A four-season addition includes full insulation, high-efficiency double or triple-pane glass, and dedicated heating and cooling, such as an extension of your HVAC system or a mini-split. A three-season room uses lighter framing and minimal insulation, which makes it less comfortable during cold winter months. Choosing between them comes down to whether you want daily year-round square footage or a budget-conscious, enclosed seasonal space.
acceptedAnswer.description: A four-season sunroom includes full insulation and HVAC integration for year-round living, while a three-season room lacks climate control and is built for spring through autumn use.
